description: We are a passionate and creative team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our team researched NASA's InSight lander, Opportunity rover, and Ingenuity helicopter. We combined scientific research with creative storytelling, wrote engaging stories, and developed a website to present our work. We chose this challenge to showcase our imagination, creativity, and teamwork. Through collaboration and dedication, we successfully completed our project.
summary: Mars Edu AI (Smart Mars Education) is an interactive educational website designed to introduce children and teenagers aged 10 to 15 to Mars, NASA robots, and space missions. The main goal of this project is to make learning about space science easier, more exciting, and more enjoyable through modern technology, interactive activities, and creative storytelling. The website combines scientific information, educational images, animated robotic characters, interactive games, and a space assistant to create a fun learning environment. Students can explore Mars, discover famous space missions, interact with a friendly robot, and improve their scientific knowledge while developing curiosity, creativity, and an interest in space exploration.
details:
1. Project Overview and How It Works

Mars Edu AI is an interactive, bilingual educational website designed to make Mars exploration and space science more accessible, engaging, and enjoyable for children and teenagers. The project combines scientific information, creative storytelling, educational games, and interactive technology to provide a learning experience that goes beyond traditional reading methods.

The website introduces four important NASA Mars missions: InSight, Opportunity, Ingenuity, and Phoenix. It explains their scientific objectives and discoveries through accessible explanations, educational visuals, and imaginative stories. Users can also explore a timeline of Mars exploration and learn about the creators of the project.

One of the website's main features is the "Little Mars Robot," an animated virtual character that interacts with users through text commands, voice recognition, animations, emotional reactions, and customizable appearances. Users can change the robot's colors and outfits, making the experience more personalized and entertaining.

Mars Edu AI also includes three educational games: a NASA science quiz, a constellation identification game, and a planet-name guessing game. These activities encourage users to test their knowledge and learn through participation.

Another important feature is the NASA Assistant, which answers space-related questions using a built-in offline knowledge system. Rather than relying on a live artificial intelligence model or an external API, the assistant uses predefined educational information to provide responses.

The website supports Persian and English, text-to-speech, voice recognition, adjustable font sizes, high-contrast mode, and simplified reading options to accommodate different learning preferences and accessibility needs.

2. Benefits of the Project

The main benefit of Mars Edu AI is making scientific information easier to understand while encouraging younger audiences to develop an interest in astronomy, technology, and space exploration.

By combining scientific explanations with storytelling, interactive games, colorful visuals, and animated characters, the website offers an educational experience that encourages active participation rather than passive reading.

Educational quizzes help users review scientific concepts, while the NASA Assistant encourages independent exploration by allowing students to ask questions about space-related topics. The Little Mars Robot increases engagement through interactive communication, animations, and personalization.

Accessibility was another important priority. Features such as bilingual content, text-to-speech, adjustable text sizes, high contrast, and simplified reading help make the website more usable for students with different needs and learning preferences.

The project also encourages curiosity, creativity, problem-solving, and the development of foundational STEM knowledge.

3. Intended Impact of the Project

Mars Edu AI aims to inspire children and teenagers to become more interested in space science, scientific discovery, and STEM education.

The project seeks to make complex astronomical concepts more approachable by presenting scientific knowledge through interactive and entertaining activities. Instead of viewing space exploration as a difficult or distant subject, students can engage with real NASA missions through stories, educational challenges, and interactive tools.

Another intended impact is to support independent learning. By encouraging users to ask questions, explore scientific information, and participate in educational games, Mars Edu AI aims to help students develop curiosity and confidence in learning about science.

The project also aims to reduce language and accessibility barriers by providing Persian and English content alongside adaptable reading and interaction features.

In the long term, Mars Edu AI hopes to motivate young learners to explore astronomy, engineering, programming, and other STEM-related fields, potentially inspiring future scientists, researchers, and innovators.

4. Tools, Technologies, and Development Process

Mars Edu AI was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

HTML provides the website's structure and educational content. CSS is responsible for the space-themed visual design, colorful interface, animations, and responsive layouts. JavaScript powers the interactive features, educational games, NASA Assistant, and Little Mars Robot.

Browser technologies, including the Web Speech API, were used to implement text-to-speech and voice recognition. Local Storage allows the website to remember the robot's selected outfit, while browser-based audio technology supports background music.

Artificial intelligence tools assisted the development process in several areas, including brainstorming, website design, coding, image creation, video editing, subtitle preparation, text improvement, and scientific research.

However, the NASA Assistant within the website operates through a built-in offline question-and-answer system rather than a direct connection to a live AI model.

The project was designed as a browser-based educational experience, allowing users to access its main content and activities without installing specialized software or using dedicated hardware.

5. Creativity and Innovation

Mars Edu AI combines space education, storytelling, interactive technology, and entertainment within a single educational platform.

One of its most distinctive creative elements is the Little Mars Robot, which transforms an ordinary educational website into a more interactive experience. Through animations, emotional reactions, voice interactions, and customizable outfits, the robot provides a playful character that users can interact with while exploring the website.

Another creative aspect is the presentation of real NASA missions through imaginative stories and accessible scientific explanations. This approach helps transform historical space missions into engaging educational experiences.

The project also uses interactive quizzes, constellation challenges, and planet-related games to make learning more participatory and enjoyable.

Its combination of Persian and English language options, accessibility tools, educational storytelling, and interactive features offers multiple ways for students to engage with scientific information.

The project's innovation lies not in inventing an entirely new technology, but in thoughtfully integrating existing web technologies and educational approaches into a cohesive, personalized, and engaging space-learning platform.

6. Factors Considered During Development

During the development of Mars Edu AI, our team considered several important factors: scientific accuracy, educational effectiveness, accessibility, ease of use, visual engagement, and technical practicality.

Scientific accuracy was important because the website introduces real NASA missions and scientific discoveries. The team aimed to communicate this information in clear, age-appropriate language while maintaining its educational value.

User engagement was another major consideration. We incorporated interactive games, animated characters, colorful illustrations, and storytelling to make the learning process more enjoyable for children and teenagers.

Accessibility and inclusivity also influenced the design. The website includes Persian and English language options, adjustable font sizes, text-to-speech, high-contrast mode, and simplified reading features to support a wider range of users.

We also considered technical accessibility by using common web technologies and creating a browser-based experience that does not require specialized equipment.

Finally, the team considered the balance between entertainment and education. Our goal was to ensure that interactive features support scientific learning rather than distract from it.

Overall, Mars Edu AI aims to demonstrate how accessible web technologies, creative storytelling, and interactive educational tools can work together to make space science more approachable, inclusive, and inspiring for the next generation of learners.
